headline: US Third-Quarter GDP Growth Revised Up to 4.3% as Inflation Reaches Three-Year High
summary: US gross domestic product growth for the third quarter was revised upward to an annualized 4.3% driven by consumer spending and investment, while the Fed's preferred inflation gauge hit a three-year high.
why: Quarterly GDP revisions and core inflation gauges provide critical macroeconomic signals for monetary policymakers assessing economic overheating and interest rate paths.

impacts.name: S&P 500
impacts.why: Stronger GDP and rising inflation can influence expectations for tighter Federal Reserve monetary policy.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Upward revisions to economic growth combined with multi-year highs in inflation measures heighten expectations of prolonged monetary tightening.
